video_title: Kalshi’s Plan to Build the Largest Exchange on Earth
gist: John Wang, who runs Kalshi's crypto, commodities and perpetuals business, lays out how the regulated onshore exchange is diversifying away from sports: crypto prediction markets are already 20-30% of exchange volume with claimed 90% category share, its CFTC-approved perpetual futures product did an order of magnitude more first-month volume than any prediction market, and commodities markets grew 100x in days. He argues the endgame is dragging the OTC and structured-products industry into lit markets to become the largest exchange on the planet, and claims Kalshi is now 4-5x larger than Poly Market overall and 10x in crypto volumes.

themes.theme: Crypto as Kalshi's Second Business Line

insights.claim: Crypto is Kalshi's second-largest business line behind sports, and Kalshi claims roughly 90% market share of crypto prediction markets.
insights.speaker: John Wang
insights.so_what: Crypto price prediction is a far bigger revenue leg for Kalshi than outside observers assume, so crypto volatility cycles are a direct driver of Kalshi's economics.
insights.quote: crypto is our second largest business line behind sports. Um we have 90% market share in the crypto predictions world.

insights.claim: Coinbase, Robin Hood crypto and Phantom route their users' prediction-market orders and trades through Kalshi, making Kalshi a B2B liquidity venue embedded inside crypto consumer apps rather than only a destination site.
insights.speaker: John Wang
insights.so_what: Distribution-partner order flow means Kalshi captures volume growth at Coinbase/Robinhood/Phantom without paying retail CAC — a moat competitors must replicate deal by deal.

insights.claim: Kalshi is explicitly not an onchain company today and says current US regulation is incompatible with going onchain, though the company expects to move that direction in several years as US legislation evolves.
insights.speaker: John Wang
insights.so_what: Anyone modeling Kalshi as a future onchain settlement layer should treat that as a multi-year regulatory-dependent option, not a roadmap item.

insights.claim: Kalshi frames its crypto prediction markets as functionally competing with Binance, Coinbase and Kraken, on the logic that those centralized exchanges are ultimately just venues for users to trade the price of crypto.
insights.speaker: John Wang
insights.so_what: Reframes the competitive set: prediction markets are taking share from spot exchange trading fees, not only from sportsbooks.

insights.claim: Crypto prediction markets travel across borders better than US-specific event markets because Bitcoin and ETH are globally recognized reference assets, alongside cricket and World Cup markets as the other proven international adoption drivers.
insights.speaker: John Wang
insights.so_what: Crypto and global sports are the wedge products for prediction-market international expansion; localized political/economic markets require country-by-country market creation.

themes.theme: Onshore Regulated Strategy and International Expansion

insights.claim: Kalshi is open in 140 countries and crypto/stablecoin rails are the only deposit and withdrawal rail it accepts for international users, because it is the most frictionless way to convert local currency into the US dollars the exchange accepts.
insights.speaker: John Wang
insights.so_what: Kalshi's international growth is a direct volume driver for stablecoin issuance and on/off-ramp businesses — a concrete non-speculative stablecoin demand channel.
insights.quote: The crypto rail is the only rail that we currently accept um for people to come into platform uh put their money in because we found it's the most frictionless way to get like you know global monetary access

insights.claim: Kalshi's international expansion strategy is to embed its prediction markets inside each country's largest incumbent broker rather than acquire users directly, with signed deals including Wealth Simple in Canada and XP, the largest broker in Brazil.
insights.speaker: John Wang
insights.so_what: Each broker deal can unlock an entire country's trader base overnight — watch broker announcements as the leading indicator of Kalshi's international volume step-changes.

insights.claim: The Circle/Tether analogy for Kalshi versus Poly Market breaks down on product, because stablecoins sell a single global product (the US dollar) with acute offshore demand, whereas prediction markets must create locally relevant questions for each country and group of people.
insights.speaker: John Wang
insights.so_what: Undermines the assumption that the offshore prediction market will out-grow the onshore one the way Tether out-grew Circle; distribution, not regulatory arbitrage, is the binding constraint.

insights.claim: Kalshi operates with roughly 180 employees, which the company estimates is 20-40x smaller headcount than comparable regulated firms like Coinbase or Circle, and it attributes its shipping velocity to that leanness.
insights.speaker: John Wang
insights.so_what: Extreme revenue-per-employee leverage is the core of the bull case on Kalshi's private valuation versus incumbent regulated exchanges.
insights.quote: we have a team of around 180 people. Um, which is probably like 20 to 40x smaller in terms of headcount than these other types of companies.

insights.claim: Kalshi had to sue the CFTC to legalize prediction markets and separately pushed to legalize perpetual futures onshore, meaning its regulatory wins are litigated precedents rather than granted permissions.
insights.speaker: John Wang
insights.so_what: Kalshi holds first-mover legal precedent that competitors inherit but did not pay for — the durable question is how fast rivals free-ride on it.
insights.quote: For prediction markets, we actually had to sue the CFTC.

insights.claim: The steelman for the onshore regulated route is that only a regulated entity can run Facebook and Instagram paid ads, buy billboards, appear on the app store, and integrate with large brokers — the only way to reach the roughly 99% of the addressable market that will not use VPNs or no-KYC offshore venues.
insights.speaker: John Wang
insights.so_what: Regulatory status is a distribution asset, not just a compliance cost — the marginal user for both prediction markets and perps is unreachable offshore.

insights.claim: Kalshi operates what it calls the first regulated perpetual futures exchange in the US, giving retail a perps app on the app store with no VPN required and giving US institutions a compliant way to access the instrument.
insights.speaker: John Wang
insights.so_what: Onshore perps open a previously walled-off US retail and institutional pool to an instrument that until now only offshore venues could serve.

insights.claim: The CFTC approval of Kalshi's Bitcoin perpetual contract effectively approved crypto as an asset class and established the risk-model framework that now lets Kalshi self-certify new crypto perps, which it has used to list over a dozen including ETH, HYPE, Solana, Zcash, Near, SUI, Doge and XRP.
insights.speaker: John Wang
insights.so_what: Listing new crypto perps is now a low-friction internal process for Kalshi, so expect rapid asset expansion and altcoin listing as a recurring catalyst.

insights.claim: Kalshi has filed with the CFTC for gold and silver perpetuals expected within weeks, using a separate 40.3 filing per asset class, with further non-crypto asset classes planned after metals.
insights.speaker: John Wang
insights.so_what: A near-dated, checkable catalyst: regulated onshore metals perps would be the first real test of Kalshi's RWA perp thesis.

insights.claim: Roughly half of Hyperliquid's volume now comes from real-world assets, and Kalshi's thesis is that the liquidity center for RWAs is US retail and US institutions — an audience offshore RWA perp venues cannot legally serve.
insights.speaker: John Wang
insights.so_what: If RWA perps are the growth frontier and the underlying liquidity is US-domiciled, a regulated onshore venue has structural advantage over offshore incumbents in that category.
insights.quote: I think around half of their volume nowadays is from these real world assets

insights.claim: Kalshi caps crypto perp leverage at about 6x, and its analysis of onchain and other perp platforms shows only 20-30% of users trade above that level while most trade between 2x and 4x, so the cap sacrifices less flow than assumed; non-crypto perps will carry much higher limits comparable to existing RWA perp venues.
insights.speaker: John Wang
insights.so_what: Kills the standard objection that regulated perps can't compete on leverage — the excluded cohort is a minority of users, though likely a disproportionate share of volume.
insights.quote: only like 20 to 30% of users trade above like our per uh leverage limit which is like 6x. Most traders we actually find they trade between 2 to 4x.

insights.claim: Kalshi claims lower perp fees than Binance and Hyperliquid at every tier, and says a six-figure order size can be filled without excessive slippage on its book.
insights.speaker: John Wang
insights.so_what: Price and depth claims are directly falsifiable — verify fee schedules and book depth before accepting that regulated perps are execution-neutral.
insights.quote: compared to like Binance or um like a hyperlid um we have lower fees at every tier currently.

insights.claim: Kalshi is internally pushing for spot markets and non-cash collateral such as Bitcoin margining, but says the unlock is regulatory rather than technical.
insights.speaker: John Wang
insights.so_what: Spot plus perps plus tokenized underlying is the combination rivals like Lighter are targeting; watch for regulatory approvals that would let Kalshi assemble the same stack.

insights.claim: Kalshi is cross-pollinating its two products by injecting prediction-market odds on Bitcoin price into the perp interface and repackaging perps as 'up or down' rather than long/short, which it says materially helps first-time perp traders.
insights.speaker: John Wang
insights.so_what: The prediction-market user base is Kalshi's cheapest acquisition funnel for perps — a distribution advantage pure perp DEXs cannot copy.

themes.theme: Insider Trading and Market Integrity Economics

insights.claim: Kalshi's stated reason for banning insider trading is market structure rather than ethics: toxic flow from informed traders causes market makers to pull quotes, which destroys liquidity and therefore destroys the price signal the market exists to produce.
insights.speaker: John Wang
insights.so_what: The clearest articulation of why prediction-market scale and information purity are in tension — surveillance intensity is a liquidity input, not a compliance overhead.
insights.quote: once you have a lot of toxic flow of like informed traders um coming in market makers aren't going to quote anymore liquidity providers are going to pull their quotes um and therefore like no one will have a liquid market to trade against and then you won't have a signal anyways.

insights.claim: Kalshi maintains surveillance lists of politicians, campaign staff, sports team employees and peripheral associates, sourced partly from third-party vendors that already serve sports betting companies and equity insider-trading surveillance.
insights.speaker: John Wang
insights.so_what: An off-the-shelf surveillance vendor stack lowers the compliance barrier for new entrants, weakening integrity infrastructure as a defensive moat.

insights.claim: Kalshi layers its own market-level rules on top of the regulatory definition of insider trading, defining and flagging it per market on the UI — for example barring members of Congress and politically associated persons from its political markets while allowing them to trade sports.
insights.speaker: John Wang
insights.so_what: Exchange-level rulemaking is currently filling a regulatory vacuum; any CFTC codification would standardize rules Kalshi already imposes and erode its self-policing differentiation.

insights.claim: Kalshi publicly supports formal regulation of insider trading in prediction markets because codification would simply enshrine practices it already runs voluntarily, giving it clarity at no incremental cost.
insights.speaker: John Wang
insights.so_what: Incumbent-favoring regulation: rules Kalshi already meets become a compliance cost that new offshore-native entrants must newly absorb.

insights.claim: Legitimate edge in prediction markets increasingly comes from obsessive domain immersion and AI-built research systems rather than private information, illustrated by a Billboard-charts YouTuber known as Grande Top 10 who consistently profits in Kalshi's music chart markets.
insights.speaker: John Wang
insights.so_what: AI-assisted research lowers the cost of legitimate alpha in niche event markets — a real, currently uncrowded retail edge.

insights.claim: Permitting even a small amount of insider trading to maximize information would push prediction markets back toward being academic play-money thought experiments rather than a multi-billion-dollar liquid asset class, according to Kalshi's rebuttal to the Robin Hanson-style information argument.
insights.speaker: John Wang
insights.so_what: Sets the ceiling on futarchy-style visions: the commercially scaled prediction market and the maximal-information prediction market are structurally different products.

themes.theme: Volume Mix Shift Away From Sports

insights.claim: Kalshi's crypto prediction markets alone are now roughly 20-30% of total exchange volume, excluding politics and economics, which Kalshi uses to reject the characterization that it is primarily a sports business.
insights.speaker: John Wang
insights.so_what: Contradicts the widely cited 70-80% sports share figure for prediction markets and reprices Kalshi as a diversified derivatives venue rather than a DraftKings competitor.
insights.quote: I think they're you know 20 to 30% of total exchange volume now and that's just for crypto

insights.claim: Kalshi's perpetual futures product did an order of magnitude more volume in its first month than any of its prediction markets have done since launch.
insights.speaker: John Wang
insights.so_what: Perps, not event contracts, may become Kalshi's dominant volume line — which changes the comparable set and the fee model used to value the company.

insights.claim: Kalshi's newly launched commodities prediction markets grew at 100x within their first few days relative to the equivalent launch period for its crypto markets, with gold, silver and oil drawing the interest.
insights.speaker: John Wang
insights.so_what: The fastest-growing category at Kalshi right now is commodities, suggesting playbook transfer from crypto is working and the next growth leg is non-sports.
insights.quote: they've grown at a rate a rate of 100x um within the first few days um of compared to like when we first launched our crypto markets

insights.claim: Kalshi projects that as commodities add roughly another 20% category share and perps scale, sports will fall to only 20-30% of exchange volume.
insights.speaker: John Wang
insights.so_what: A falsifiable forecast for the mix shift — if sports share drops as predicted, the CME-comparable valuation frame gets more defensible than the DraftKings one.

insights.claim: Kalshi is productizing political markets into tradeable weighted indices, including a product it calls KPAL described as an S&P 500 for the US political landscape, taking a research-oriented Bloomberg-like posture rather than a betting posture.
insights.speaker: John Wang
insights.so_what: Indexation is how event contracts become institutionally consumable benchmarks — watch whether index products attract macro fund flows.
insights.quote: we have this thing called KPAL which is kind of like the S&P 500 but the US political landscape

themes.theme: Institutional Capital and the OTC-to-Lit Thesis

insights.claim: Kalshi's core institutional thesis is that moving the OTC and structured-products industries out of bilaterally negotiated dark markets and into lit, openly traded prediction markets expands the addressable market and activity by roughly 10x.
insights.speaker: John Wang
insights.so_what: This is the actual bull case for a CME-scale valuation — the target pool is structured products, not sportsbook handle.
insights.quote: we can for the institutional world I think we can take this like the entire OTC industry bring it into prediction markets take the entire structured products industry bring it into prediction markets

insights.claim: Kalshi's first block trade was a Houston-based environmental hedge fund hedging whether a specific price would be reached in California's May carbon allowance auctions, demonstrating that institutions can already get bespoke, precise hedges built on request and then priced by the open market.
insights.speaker: John Wang
insights.so_what: Rebuts the 'prediction markets are too blunt to hedge with' objection with a concrete bespoke-contract mechanism institutions can request today.
insights.quote: Our first block trade, for example, was by um some Houstonbased environmental hedge fund, and they wanted to hedge against whether a specific price for May carbon allowance auctions in California would be be would occur.

insights.claim: Margin on event contracts is Kalshi's single most requested institutional feature and is not yet shipped, with perps currently serving as the capital-efficient substitute for institutions.
insights.speaker: John Wang
insights.so_what: The binding constraint on institutional prediction-market adoption is capital efficiency; margin on event contracts would be the unlock to watch for.
insights.quote: getting margin on prediction markets is probably our top requested feature for um our event contracts

insights.claim: Real commercial hedging is already occurring on Kalshi's weather and event markets, including an ice cream shop and dozens of bars that hedged World Cup free-drink promotions, plus seven- and eight-figure block trades on CLARITY Act passage odds.
insights.speaker: John Wang
insights.so_what: Promotional and legislative-risk hedging are early proof of non-speculative demand — the seed of an insurance-adjacent revenue line.

insights.claim: Kalshi positions itself as a CME or NYSE analogue that also owns the direct trader relationship the way Robin Hood and IBKR do, and is plugged into essentially all major US broker platforms and institutional trading terminals.
insights.speaker: John Wang
insights.so_what: Combining exchange economics with broker-style direct customer ownership is the structural argument for why Kalshi could out-earn a pure exchange multiple.
insights.quote: That that is our ultimate goal is to be the largest exchange um on the planet

insights.claim: Politics is the category where Kalshi claims true monopoly utility, arguing hedge funds cannot obtain political exposure anywhere else and therefore need a prediction-market position for portfolio risk parameters and pricing efficiency.
insights.speaker: John Wang
insights.so_what: Political event contracts are the least substitutable product Kalshi sells — the most likely first institutional mandate line item.

themes.theme: Kalshi vs Poly Market Competitive Dynamics

insights.claim: Kalshi says it has grown to be four to five times larger than Poly Market overall and ten times larger in crypto volumes, and that the two firms' year-long pattern of mirrored partnership announcements has subsided over roughly the past six months.
insights.speaker: John Wang
insights.so_what: If verified, the duopoly is resolving into a clear leader, which would reprice both companies' private valuations and reduce partnership bidding wars.
insights.quote: we've really um grown to be like four to five times larger at least in crypto. We're 10 times larger than them um in volumes.

insights.claim: Third parties including sports leagues and even creators with 20k followers exploited the Kalshi-Poly Market rivalry to bid up partnership deals and sign both platforms, which Kalshi says led to deals getting overbid and money burned, and which has largely stopped in the last six months.
insights.speaker: John Wang
insights.so_what: Sponsorship and partnership cost inflation in prediction markets appears to be deflating — margin tailwind for the leader.
insights.quote: we haven't seen as much of that in the past six months.

insights.claim: Kalshi claims category firsts over Poly Market in three specific areas: it was first to rip a compute forward curve and grow compute markets, its perp exchange is regulated and released while Poly Market's is still in beta, and it has more institutional block-trade and hedging adoption.
insights.speaker: John Wang
insights.so_what: Compute forward curves and regulated perps are the two differentiators to track as evidence of durable separation rather than temporary lead.
insights.quote: we're the first to rip a compute forward curve and grow our compute markets

insights.claim: Kalshi launched Kalshi Pro, which it describes as the first official prediction-market trading terminal released by a prediction market, aimed at matching the interfaces of brokerages like Moomoo and tastytrade to attract advanced traders.
insights.speaker: John Wang
insights.so_what: Terminal-grade tooling is how a retail venue climbs into professional flow — a prerequisite for the institutional volume Kalshi is targeting.
